spec_match.rationale: The feature has no web API; the page exercises exactly the web-reachable members of Chromium's ClientSideDetectionType enum (csd.proto) with their real APIs, and states that scans/verdicts are unobservable.

interactive.rationale: Seven cards call real APIs (requestFullscreen, keyboard.lock/unlock, requestPointerLock, vibrate, clipboard.writeText, Notification.requestPermission, a cc-number form) with genuine return values; live active-signal tally; release-all.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Delivers the promised real calls and no verdict.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported APIs reported per card; rejections shown with error names; keyboard lock labelled 'requested' outside fullscreen; pointer lock auto-releases; permission already decided is explained.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (Playwright) at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch; console and network clean; 0px horizontal overflow (after fixes); feature-level conformance panel rendered 4 pass / 0 fail / 3 blocked. The scan itself is never observable from a page, so no verdict evidence exists by design. All seven actions exercised at both viewports: fullscreen entered/exited, keyboard.lock resolved, pointer lock locked then auto-released at 3 s, vibrate→true, writeText resolved (permission granted in the test context), requestPermission→denied (headless), release-all left 0 active signals. Partial: real Chrome UI behaviour (Esc-hold bubble, notification prompt, chrome://safe-browsing logs) needs a headed browser.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts fullscreen really entered (or the fallback really did not), keyboard lock/unlock pairing, and a clean release-all.

design_system.rationale: Tokens only; active state rose, inactive emerald-dark on ivory.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons with descriptive names, live tally and role=log, pointer lock never left captured.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Both classes verified; on real phones Keyboard/Pointer Lock are absent and the cards say so instead of failing silently.

openQuestions.title: Observe chrome://safe-browsing in a headed ESB profile
openQuestions.detail: Confirm which of these calls produce client-side detection pings in the chrome://safe-browsing log for an Enhanced Protection profile, and record the tab name per Chrome version.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce discrete outcomes in polite status/log regions; native labelled controls; visible focus.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Outcomes in role=status/role=log; native buttons, radios, checkboxes with visible labels and focus-visible outlines.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Collapse grids on narrow viewports, wrap long tokens, keep 44px targets.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Single-column below 760-900px, overflow-wrap:anywhere on code and enum names, 44px controls; measured 0px overflow at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.query: fullscreen and keyboard lock exit instructions accessible
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Manage focus on context changes and never trap keyboard users; provide a visible, operable way out.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Focus moves to the in-fullscreen Exit button; exit instructions are visible inside the fullscreen element; only a specific key list is locked; pointer lock auto-releases after 3 s.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Search returned accessibility/dialog guides; no fullscreen-specific guide exists, so the generic focus-management and no-keyboard-trap rules were applied.

summary: Real calls to every web-reachable scam-check trigger type, with honest unobservable-verdict framing.
